original_question: For a pair (C, G) satisfying condition (N), what groups can occur as the second lower ramification group G_2?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in the section "p-groups as automorphism groups of curves in characteristic p": for a pair (C,G) satisfying condition (N), is the second lower ramification group G_2 necessarily abelian?
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main objects of the paper’s question: a pair (C,G) under condition (N) and the second lower ramification group G_2. It also correctly focuses on the structural possibilities for G_2, which is exactly the local group-theoretic invariant singled out in the paper’s opening conjecture and its immediate follow-up results.
missing_details: The ambient field should be specified: k is an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0.
The curve should be specified: C is a connected nonsingular projective curve over k of genus g>=2.
The group should be specified: G is a p-subgroup of Aut_k(C).
Condition (N) should be stated explicitly as |G|/g > 2p/(p-1).
The ramification-theoretic setting should be made explicit: C -> C/G has a unique ramification point, and G_2 is the second lower ramification group at that point.
The paper’s nearest official target is not a full classification of all abstract groups that can occur as G_2; it is the sharper question of whether G_2 must be abelian.

The nearby context includes Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 as partial evidence around Conjecture 1.1, so a stand-alone reformulation should reflect that the paper is asking for an abelianity statement, not an unrestricted classification problem.
The role of lower numbering should be explicit, since 'second ramification group' is otherwise ambiguous.
The fact that G is the wild inertia group G_1 at the unique ramification point is part of the setup used in the paper’s formulation.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, let C/k be a connected nonsingular projective curve of genus g>=2, and let G be a p-subgroup of Aut_k(C) such that (C,G) satisfies condition (N), namely |G|/g > 2p/(p-1). If infinity is the unique ramification point of the cover C -> C/G, so that G=G_1 is the wild inertia group at infinity, must the second lower ramification group G_2 at infinity be abelian?
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper’s opening discussion of the second lower ramification group under condition (N), but it is broader than the paper’s actual formulation. The nearest official statement is Conjecture 1.1, which asks for abelianity of G_2, not a complete classification of all possible abstract groups G_2. Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 are the immediate nearby results that support and narrow this conjectural picture, so the refined question should stay at that level of scope rather than expand into a general classification problem.
